doc.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Upcoming QE II trip and Antonio Hart, Leo Wright
summary: Plans to sail with the Dizzy Gillespie Sextet; talk of Antonio Hart and Leo Wright's versatility in Berlin.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Very interesting. What’s coming up in the near future for you?

Next week — Paris, London, and then we’re going to fly over, I’m going to fly over to Paris because I have to do business in Paris and then I’m going to London because we’re coming back on the QE II and we’re playing for the whole way back with the Dizzy Gillespie Sextet.
And who is in that group now?
This time will be Terrell Stafford, Antonio Hart, I think Renee Rosnes, John Lee and Dennis Mackrel. And they’re giving us the best cabins on the boat.
All right. I like Antonio Hart. He reminds me of Cannonball some, who was my absolute hero.

He’s a talented guy. This guy has so much talent, man, he’s got to find some way — you know, hold him. He’s brilliant man. He knows so much. He loves music so much that he just, you know, it’s probably hard for him to relate to too much outside of music. And it’s been wonderful working with him because he’s a very serious — whatever he plays he’s very serious about it. He plays a lot of different styles you know. But see when I was in Berlin I worked with Leo Wright. Leo Wright and Carmell Jones. We were in one of the radio bands together. And Leo could play every style of music that there is, and played © Fillius Jazz Archive -23-

them all with conviction. It was one of the most fantastic things I ever saw. He could play country-western, he could play the blues, he could play old style, he could play traditional, he could play straight ahead, he could play like Trane. It was unbelievable. And the guys were actually mad at him because the guy could play so many styles they hired him for everything. He could read everything in sight. Tony’s got a lot of that in him.
